rationale: CROSS-FILE ANCESTRY, TWO HOPS UP (java lane, 2026-11-17). This fixture lives in a sub-directory, so the runner gives it a real project index (JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC, complete=true). `Use` calls `inherited()`, declared by `Base` - its grandparent, in another file; the direct parent `Middle` declares nothing. The owner channel's in-file walk reads `index.typeScopesByName`, so it sees `Use`'s parents, finds `Middle` among the project's members with no `inherited`, and previously STOPPED there: a member inherited two or more levels up through a cross-file parent was refused (`missing`, never wrong). The analyzer now falls back to the project's own ancestry (`projectIndex.typeBases`) ONLY when the in-file walk found nothing, so no row that resolved before can change, and it still requires EXACTLY ONE declaration across the chain. NEGATIVE CONTROL: `notInherited()` is declared nowhere, so it must not appear - the fallback must not manufacture a resolution.

forbidRelationships.comment: declared nowhere: the cross-file fallback must not invent a resolution
